solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Work confined to terribly precise submarine equipment

indicators.note: the work abbreviation is shut up inside the rearranged letters, confined within them
terribly signals that the letters of precise are badly jumbled

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Some job is being cooped up in horribly exacting gear aboard a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the musical opus, abbreviated; 'terribly' yields PERISCE, which 'confined to' then wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine raises this viewing tube above the water to see the surface while submerged.

clue.text: Meeting prisoner of war — how amazing!

parts.note: POW is the standard abbreviation for a prisoner of war
wow is an exclamation of amazement

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to be meeting a captured soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is an informal word for a conference or discussion, originally a Native American gathering.

clue.text: Get up around noon, initially to clean

indicators.note: around says the rising word goes round the next letter

parts.note: to rise is to get up out of bed

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of noon

explanation.surface: A lazy sleeper rises about midday, at first just to wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to clean something with water, a synonym in verb form.

clue.text: For example, cricket side gets a run with a bye

parts.note: say can mean for example, as in 'take a fruit, say, an apple'
on, or leg side, is one half of a cricket field
R is the scoring abbreviation for a run in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket team picks up a run courtesy of a bye, an extra not hit by the bat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the half of the field the batsman faces with their legs; a bye is a run scored without the bat touching the ball, but here it is goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Sayonara is a Japanese farewell, used in English as an informal way to say goodbye.

clue.text: Cuckoo say, the correct bird

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone names the cuckoo as an example of the right bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like the bird in question, but it is the anagram signal for SAY THE CORRECT.
explanation.definitionFit: The oystercatcher is a black-and-white wading shorebird with a long orange bill.

clue.text: Eve's first lair, Biblical garden

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word Eve's

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: Eve's original home was the garden of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis places Adam and Eve in this paradise garden before the Fall.

clue.text: Part of a curve, and rather circular for starters

indicators.note: for starters means take the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson: a portion of a curve, rather round in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a section of a curved line such as a circle.

clue.text: After refurbishment, do cater for design style

indicators.note: refurbishment remakes something, so the letters of do cater are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once a venue is refitted, it serves food in a particular decorative look.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s in architecture and design.

clue.text: Shout about that woman's fruit

indicators.note: about places the shout around the word for that woman

parts.note: to cry out is to shout
her is the possessive for that woman, as in her book

explanation.surface: Someone yells about the fruit belonging to some woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry is a small round stone fruit, red or black, an example of the class.

clue.text: Reversal of some elementary knowledge, askew

indicators.note: Reversal says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A setback in basic learning leaves things a little crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonky is informal for crooked or lopsided, a synonym of askew.

clue.text: Respect reforms as royal staff

indicators.note: reforms means the letters of respect are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Deference reshapes the people serving a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal staff' suggests palace servants, but it is the ornamental rod a monarch holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the ornamental rod carried by a monarch as a symbol of sovereignty.

clue.text: Shrub found in hole, and eroding

indicators.note: found in says the answer lies inside the words hole, and eroding

explanation.surface: A plant is discovered growing in a crumbling hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous evergreen flowering bush of warm climates.

clue.text: Good listener finding equipment

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: An attentive confidant turns up some kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is a general word for kit or apparatus, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Entirety destroyed for ever

definitions.note: a phrase meaning endless time, used here as a noun phrase for the time without end

indicators.note: destroyed means the word entirety is wrecked and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: The whole thing is ruined permanently.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is infinite time; 'for ever' names that endless span, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Injured Briton came to collect old skin lotion

indicators.note: to collect means the scrambled letters gather up the abbreviation for old
injured says the words Briton came are damaged and their letters reordered

explanation.surface: A hurt Brit arrived to fetch an old ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' rearranges BRITON CAME to EMBRCATION, and 'to collect' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrocation is a liquid rubbed on the body to ease aching muscles, a medicinal liniment.

clue.text: Milton tormented about love illuminated at night

indicators.note: about places the scrambled name around the letter for love
tormented says the poet's name is twisted into another order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: The poet Milton agonises over love by night's light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tormented' rearranges MILTON to MONLIT, and 'about' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonlit describes a scene lit by the moon, which shines only after dark.

clue.text: Chess piece — king wrong thing!

parts.note: K is the chess notation for king

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of thing come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A chess player complains the king is the wrong piece to move.
explanation.definitionFit: This chess piece moves in an L shape and is usually carved as a horse's head.

clue.text: Scattered boxes on top of everything

parts.note: to spar is to box, so boxes gives spars

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of everything, the top of a down entry

explanation.surface: Containers are strewn on top of all the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like containers but is the verb: spars as a boxer does.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly spread or scattered, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Gaseous element — one confused with nitrogen

indicators.note: confused says the letters of one are muddled

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry student mixes up one gas with nitrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, element number ten, used in glowing signs.

clue.text: Celebrity's cool rocket

parts.note: a celebrity is a star, and the possessive gives star's
hip means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: A famous person owns a trendy spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A starship is a spacecraft for interstellar travel, a kind of rocket in science fiction.

clue.text: Tongue behind top of incisors

parts.note: hind means at the back, behind

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of incisors in this down entry

explanation.surface: A tongue sits just behind the tip of the front teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' sounds anatomical next to incisors, but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is a language of northern India, and tongue is an old word for a language.

clue.text: Bit of leg — potential beef?

definitions.meaning: the fleshy back part of the lower leg
a young cow that may one day be eaten as beef

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the muscle at the back of the shin, and a young bovine animal destined for the table.

clue.text: Giant pig holding his curly appendage back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is read in reverse
holding means the pig word wraps around the appendage word

parts.note: a hog is a pig
a pig's tail is famously curly

explanation.surface: A huge pig keeps its corkscrew tail tucked behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' gives HTAILOG, which 'back' then turns round; the curly appendage is the pig's own corkscrew tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the Philistine giant slain by David, now a byword for any huge figure.

clue.text: Private pub, 'The Queen'

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A pub with a royal name, the Queen, kept exclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier or an adjective about the pub, but it means inward or personal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner can mean private or not openly shown, as in one's inner thoughts.

clue.text: Dram — little one

definitions.meaning: a small measure of spirits such as whisky

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a small shot of liquor, and a toddler or young child.

clue.text: Record when WWII ended

definitions.meaning: a vinyl single played at that many revolutions per minute
the Second World War ended in 1945, often shortened to the last two digits

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a seven-inch single spun at that speed, and the year the Second World War ended.
